note: Which blank or invisible Unicode character each app keeps. 'works' rows were checked on real accounts; 'test first' rows change with app updates.

characters.name: Hangul Filler
characters.use: Game nicknames (Free Fire, PUBG), TikTok nickname, Instagram name and bio lines

characters.name: Braille Pattern Blank
characters.use: Blank messages and comments in WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Instagram comments

characters.name: Zero-Width Space
characters.use: X (Twitter) posts, iPhone Notes; stripped by most chat apps

characters.name: Halfwidth Hangul Filler
characters.use: Fallback for name fields that reject U+3164

characters.name: Hair Space
characters.use: Survives Word, Google Docs and email

characters.name: Em Space
characters.use: Wide gaps in documents and captions

characters.name: Zero-Width Non-Joiner
characters.use: Typography; used by zero-width steganography to encode bits

characters.name: No-Break Space
characters.use: Never breaks a line; most apps still trim it

apps.note: U+200B and U+200C are stripped before sending, so the message is rejected as empty.
The username field accepts only letters, digits, dots and underscores; no blank works there.
One character is enough; several make a taller comment.
The character behind the 'invisible name' trend videos.
Usernames are a-z, 0-9, dots and underscores only; a server nickname can be blank with U+3164.
A rename costs diamonds or a rename card. One character is enough; two if the game says the name is too short.
X collapses runs of ordinary spaces; a zero-width space survives.
iMessage refuses a message that is only U+200B; use U+2800 there.
Roblox strips most fillers after updates; the username never accepts them.
Epic allows one display-name change every two weeks; test before you spend it.
